unlisted_practices: Conduct situated, prospective evaluation of clinical AI decision-support systems in realistic workflows with real end users, rather than relying on bench studies alone.
Incorporate formative situated evaluation early in the development process, before late-stage clinical evaluation.
Evaluate the human-machine combination, not the machine output alone.
Use situated co-design that actively involves clinicians and end users in AI development, exposing the algorithm's features, capabilities and limitations during design.
Design mutually tractable representations and iterative, bi-directional interaction between clinicians and AI to support convergence in decision-making.

Use the eight contextual dimensions of combination (participating agents, control relations, task overlap, temporal patterning, informational proximity, informational overlap, input influence, output representation coverage) to frame the design and evaluation of human-AI decision systems.

screen.reason: This is a framework/perspective paper introducing a relational space (contextual dimensions of combination) to guide the design and deployment of situated clinical AI systems.
